title: Closest Equal Element Queries
summary: Given a circular array nums and an array queries, for each query, find the smallest distance to another index where the value matches the queried index.
statement: Given a circular array nums and an array queries, for each query, find the smallest distance to another index where the value matches the queried index. If no match exists, return -1. The result is an array corresponding to each query.
constraints: nums is a nonempty circular array and every query is a valid index.
For each query, find another index with the same value.
Return the smallest circular index distance, or -1 if the value occurs only once.
hints: Equal-value indices form sorted circular position lists; only the predecessor and successor can be closest.
Group indices by value and binary-search each queried position within its group.
Measure modular distance to the previous and next group members; return their minimum, or -1 for a singleton group.
Any farther equal occurrence lies beyond one of these neighbors along a circular direction and cannot improve the distance.
editorial: Any farther equal occurrence lies beyond one of these neighbors along a circular direction and cannot improve the distance.

tests.explanation: Index zero is two steps from another one, index three has no other four, and index five is three circular steps from another three.
Each index is one step from the other equal value.
